question: Why is teaching patients to read food labels a great nursing skill for fat management?

options.A: It proves processed foods are dangerous
options.B: It helps them spot hidden trans and saturated fats
options.C: It guarantees quick weight loss
options.D: It means they never need to see a dietitian again

explanation: Food labels can be tricky! Teaching patients to read them empowers them to catch hidden bad fats lurking in packaged snacks.

question: A patient asks why their belly pain gets worse after eating a meal. What is the best way to explain this?

options.A: Food stretches the stomach wall, putting physical pressure on the pancreas.
options.B: Eating triggers the pancreas to release enzymes, which irritates the inflamed tissue.
options.C: Eating causes bile to back up instantly into the liver, stopping digestion.
options.D: Food particles enter the pancreatic duct directly, blocking the flow of blood.

explanation: Makes sense, right? When food enters the gut, your body tells the pancreas to pump out digestive enzymes. If the pancreas is already inflamed, sending out those juices just makes it hurt more.

question: A public health nurse inspects local drinking water sources and tracks cholera cases in a neighborhood. Which core function is the nurse performing?

options.A: Financial auditing
options.B: Assessment
options.C: Hospital accreditation
options.D: Policy development

explanation: Monitoring health status and investigating health hazards fall directly under the assessment function of public health. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h5)

question: What shape does the *Vibrio cholerae* bacterium have under a microscope?

options.A: Spherical clusters
options.B: Long branching filaments
options.C: Comma-shaped
options.D: Thick spore-forming rods

explanation: Think of a tiny punctuation mark! Vibrio cholerae is classically recognized as a curved, comma-shaped rod.

question: Which condition is commonly checked during routine school health screening?

options.A: Visual acuity
options.B: Blood clotting disorders
options.C: Bone fracture history
options.D: Surgical site infections

explanation: Vision screening is a standard part of school health checks because poor eyesight directly impacts reading and classroom learning. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h7)

question: During which step of the planning process does a nurse manager weigh the pros and cons of different staffing methods?

options.A: Premising the future
options.B: Establishing the budget
options.C: Setting objectives
options.D: Evaluating alternatives

explanation: Evaluating alternatives involves comparing the advantages and disadvantages of each proposed option before making a final choice. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why is it important to document the exact number of shocks the AED delivered during a code?

options.A: It tells the biomedical department when to throw away the machine's battery.
options.B: It provides critical data for the medical team reviewing the patient's clinical course.
options.C: It proves to the hospital administration that the nurse followed the correct protocol.
options.D: It determines how much financial charge the patient receives for equipment use.

explanation: Doctors and the healthcare team need to know how many shocks were given to understand how the patient's heart responded and plan their next steps.

question: How do convulsions and seizures relate to each other?

options.A: All seizures are convulsions, but not all convulsions are seizures
options.B: Convulsions only occur in adults, while seizures only occur in children
options.C: All convulsions are seizures, but not all seizures are convulsions
options.D: Convulsions and seizures are completely unrelated conditions

explanation: Think of it this way: every convulsion is a type of seizure because of the shaking, but some seizures happen without any body movements at all. You're mastering the basics!

question: What is the typical normal oxygen saturation range for a healthy adult breathing room air?
explanation: Healthy individuals without lung or heart disease usually maintain oxygen saturation levels between 95% and 100%. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is the key sign of a post-dural puncture headache?

options.A: It gets worse when the patient sits up and improves when lying flat
options.B: It feels like a sharp electrical shock running down both legs
options.C: It stays at the exact same intensity regardless of body position
options.D: It only occurs during the night and disappears by afternoon

explanation: You nailed it! Low fluid pressure pulls on pain-sensitive areas when upright, which eases up when the patient lies horizontal.

question: How are special senses different from general senses?

options.A: Special senses are housed in complex, distinct organs in the head
options.B: Special senses only function while a person is sleeping
options.C: General senses do not use electrical impulses to communicate
options.D: General senses are controlled entirely by the spinal cord

explanation: Unlike touch receptors that are spread all over your body, special senses like sight, taste, and hearing have their own specialized, dedicated homes in the head, like the eyes and tongue!

question: Which part of the nervous system keeps the penis in its resting, flaccid state?

options.A: Parasympathetic nervous system
options.B: Sympathetic nervous system
options.C: Enteric nervous system
options.D: Somatic motor system

explanation: You're doing great! The sympathetic system (our 'fight or flight' and resting tone manager) keeps the muscles contracted so the penis stays soft.

question: What is the main reason for nursing supervision in the hospital ward?

options.A: To ensure care meets safe and ethical standards
options.B: To discipline staff who make clinical errors
options.C: To reduce the number of working hours for nurses
options.D: To replace formal classroom nursing education

explanation: Think of supervision as a supportive guide. Its main job is to make sure patient care stays safe, proper, and of high quality!

question: Why are alternative rites of passage considered effective grassroots strategies against FGM?

options.A: They replace traditional ceremonies with strict western religious rituals
options.B: They preserve cultural celebrations of maturity while eliminating physical harm
options.C: They allow traditional cutters to continue practicing safely in hospitals
options.D: They provide direct employment for healthcare workers in rural clinics

explanation: Alternative rites honor the cultural need for a coming-of-age milestone while removing the dangerous physical cutting component. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T7#GNS312_U1_T7_h4)

question: How do hormone-producing cells in the Diffuse Neuroendocrine System (DNES) differ from traditional glands?

options.A: They consist exclusively of modified postganglionic sympathetic neurons derived from neural crest tissue
options.B: They possess specialized ducts that empty their chemical secretions directly into the lumen of the gastrointestinal tract
options.C: They lack a blood supply entirely and rely purely on local nervous system stimulation for hormone distribution
options.D: Their hormone-producing cells are scattered singly among other mucosal cell types rather than clustered in a dedicated gland

explanation: Instead of sitting together in one organ (like the thyroid), DNES cells are scattered solo across places like your gut lining, quietly sending out local chemical signals.

question: Why does stopping breastfeeding early increase a baby's chance of getting diarrhoea?

options.A: It stops the liver from storing adequate iron reserves
options.B: It forces the infant to produce too much stomach acid
options.C: It causes immediate permanent damage to the pancreas
options.D: It removes protective maternal antibodies that guard the infant gut

explanation: Breast milk is liquid gold for babies! It carries special antibodies that shield their delicate digestive system from germs while their own immune system is still growing.

question: A young woman with a history of FGM comes to the clinic with lower tummy pain and painful urination. What is a likely cause?

options.A: Excessive estrogen production
options.B: Chronic urinary tract infections from scarring
options.C: Early-onset menopause
options.D: Congenital kidney failure

explanation: You nailed it! Scarring and altered anatomy from FGM can block normal urine flow, making infections and pain much more likely.

question: What is the medical term for trouble swallowing in advanced degenerative diseases?

options.A: Apraxia
options.B: Aphasia
options.C: Dysphagia
options.D: Ataxia

explanation: Dysphagia means difficulty swallowing. Spotting this early helps us protect patients from choking or getting food in their lungs!

question: What is a major goal of financial control when it comes to hospital supplies?

options.A: Resource optimization to prevent unnecessary waste
options.B: Throwing away expired items without tracking
options.C: Hiding extra supplies in locked closets indefinitely
options.D: Buying only the most expensive brands available

explanation: A key goal is using our materials wisely so we avoid waste and keep things running without breaking the bank.

question: Why is it important for clinical nurses to understand basic legal frameworks regarding harmful practices?

options.A: To recognize mandatory reporting duties and protect vulnerable patients
options.B: To arrest individuals who bring injured patients to the hospital
options.C: To write new bills for the national legislative assembly
options.D: To act as defense attorneys during court trials for offenders

explanation: Nurses must know when the law requires reporting child abuse or imminent danger to child protection authorities. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h3)

question: How is the pathway of our sense of smell (olfaction) different from all other senses?

options.A: It completely bypasses the cerebral cortex entirely
options.B: It does not pass through the thalamus before reaching the cortex
options.C: It crosses over to the opposite side of the brain twice
options.D: It is processed entirely within the occipital lobe

explanation: Unlike sight or sound, smell signals go straight to the olfactory cortex without stopping at the thalamus relay station first. That's a classic exam favorite!

question: Why are stool softeners frequently given to patients recovering from major surgery?

options.A: They completely stop all intestinal gas and bloating
options.B: They prevent painful straining during bowel movements
options.C: They speed up the healing of abdominal skin incisions
options.D: They kill harmful bacteria hiding in the large intestine

explanation: Exactly! Keeping the stool soft saves healing surgical patients from painful bearing down and straining.

question: A new mother on the ward is bleeding heavily two hours after delivery, and her uterus feels soft and boggy. What is the likely cause?

options.A: Eclamptic seizure
options.B: Obstructed labor
options.C: Pelvic inflammatory disease
options.D: Uterine atony

explanation: When the uterus fails to contract firmly (atony), the blood vessels stay open and bleeding happens. A firm massage and oxytocics are usually our best friends here!

question: In the human female reproductive tract, where does fertilization usually happen?

options.A: Surface of the ovary
options.B: Lower third of the uterine cavity
options.C: Ampulla of the fallopian tube
options.D: Cervical canal

explanation: The ampulla is the wider middle section of the fallopian tube and provides the perfect meeting place for the swimming sperm and the released egg.

question: Which Nigerian agency leads the fight against drug trafficking and abuse?

options.A: Frsc
options.B: Nafdac
options.C: Nysc
options.D: NDLEA

explanation: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) is the main body responsible for tackling illicit drug crimes in Nigeria.

question: Which common bacterium that lives inside cells is frequently responsible for cervicitis?

options.A: Staphylococcus aureus
options.B: Escherichia coli
options.C: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
options.D: Chlamydia trachomatis

explanation: Chlamydia trachomatis is a well-known bug that loves to hide inside cervical cells and cause inflammation.

question: What is the main goal of an Infant Welfare Clinic?

options.A: Emergency trauma management
options.B: Surgical operations for newborns
options.C: Preventive care and health promotion
options.D: Inpatient hospital admission

explanation: You've got this! These clinics focus on stopping illnesses before they start through check-ups and immunizations, rather than treating severe hospital emergencies. Great job keeping kids healthy!

question: What is the primary goal of palliative care in a long-term care setting?

options.A: Curing the underlying chronic terminal disease
options.B: Eliminating the need for family involvement
options.C: Accelerating the physical dying process safely
options.D: Relieving pain and managing distressing symptoms

explanation: Wonderful job! Palliative care is all about maximizing comfort, easing heavy symptoms, and bringing peace of mind to patients with serious illnesses.

question: What is the main job of a bacteriostatic drug?

options.A: Neutralizing bacterial toxins in the blood
options.B: Stopping bacteria from multiplying
options.C: Instantly killing all bacterial cells
options.D: Destroying human white blood cells

explanation: Bacteriostatic drugs press 'pause' on bacterial growth and let the patient's immune system clean up the rest.

question: A 45-year-old Nigerian civil servant works a desk job and has central obesity. Which condition is he most at risk for?

options.A: Acute diabetic ketoacidosis
options.B: Gestational diabetes
options.C: Type 1 autoimmune diabetes
options.D: Type 2 diabetes mellitus

explanation: Sitting for long hours, lack of exercise, and belly fat are classic risk factors for Type 2 diabetes. Seeing how this connects to real life makes clinical rotations much easier!

question: Which hormone primarily stimulates sodium reabsorption in the distal nephron?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Thyroxine
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Aldosterone

explanation: Aldosterone acts on the distal tubules and collecting ducts to increase sodium and water reabsorption, raising blood volume. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T1#GNS121_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading in home care?

options.A: Proper hand hygiene
options.B: Restricting all visitors permanently
options.C: Wearing sterile gowns all day
options.D: Spraying rooms with strong perfumes

explanation: Good old-fashioned handwashing is your best defense! It removes germs and stops them from passing between you and your patients.

question: Why should a nurse designer limit a health poster to just one or two main actions?

options.A: Health workers do not have time to memorize long lists of instructions.
options.B: Paper becomes too heavy and expensive to distribute easily.
options.C: Government printing presses refuse to print more than two sentences.
options.D: Too many competing messages confuse the audience and dilute the impact.

explanation: Keep it simple! If you put too many instructions on one poster, people get overwhelmed and walk away remembering nothing.

question: Which substance must be present in a rehydration solution to help activate the SGLT1 transporter in the gut?

options.A: Glucose
options.B: Potassium
options.C: Bicarbonate
options.D: Protein

explanation: Think of glucose as a helpful partner! It teams up with sodium to attach to the SGLT1 transporter, which helps pull both molecules into the intestinal cells.

question: What structural feature makes capillaries ideally suited for gas and nutrient exchange?

options.A: They are equipped with one-way valves to prevent backflow
options.B: Their walls are only a single cell layer thick
options.C: They contain strong layers of circular smooth muscle
options.D: Their lumen has a larger diameter than any other vessel

explanation: Having a wall thickness of just one cell minimizes the diffusion distance for oxygen, nutrients, and waste products. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why is it dangerous to use traditional home remedies like forcing caustic liquids or oils down someone's throat after they swallow a poison?

options.A: Traditional remedies always cure toxic exposures faster than modern hospital drugs.
options.B: Community members refuse to visit hospitals unless accompanied by a nurse.
options.C: Practices like forcing caustic liquids or oils down the throat can worsen tissue injury and cause aspiration.
options.D: Myths prevent patients from paying their hospital bills on time.

explanation: Forcing things down can cause the chemical to burn the throat a second time on the way back up, or slip into the lungs and cause deadly pneumonia. Always educate gently against this!

question: How might a partner's attitude cause a client to stop coming for family planning?

options.A: Disapproval or secret opposition can force the client to stop using services quietly
options.B: Supportive partners always pay the clinic staff to cancel appointments
options.C: Involved partners automatically double the efficacy of oral pills
options.D: Partner involvement has no impact on clinic attendance

explanation: Fear of conflict at home can lead clients to quietly drop out. As nurses, creating a safe, confidential space helps us support them through these challenges.

question: What is the primary reason for encouraging high fluid intake after an intravenous pyelogram?

options.A: To prevent the patient from feeling hungry after fasting
options.B: To help flush the contrast dye out of the kidneys quickly
options.C: To stimulate normal bowel movements following the procedure
options.D: To replace the fluid lost during the mandatory bowel preparation

explanation: Drinking plenty of fluids dilutes any remaining dye and encourages prompt urination, protecting the kidneys from potential injury. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h6)

question: How do assistive devices and home changes mainly help a patient whose health is declining?

options.A: By completely removing the need for a nurse
options.B: By bridging the gap between needing help and safe independence
options.C: By replacing lost brain function from dementia
options.D: By curing underlying chronic illnesses

explanation: Brilliant! Tools and modifications are all about helping patients squeeze out every bit of independence they safely can.

question: Which type of surgical sponge is the largest and best for major tummy (abdominal) surgeries?

options.A: Lap sponge
options.B: Neuro patty
options.C: Gauze swab
options.D: Tonsil sponge

explanation: Lap sponges (laparotomy sponges) are large and heavy-duty, designed to handle deep abdominal operations easily.

question: Why is regular antenatal care attendance so important for catching problems like antepartum haemorrhage early?

options.A: It builds up thick blood volume reserves to prevent all shock
options.B: It completely stops the uterus from contracting before term
options.C: It allows early ultrasound identification of abnormal placental placement
options.D: It guarantees that the mother will never experience any spotting

explanation: Routine antenatal check-ups and scans help healthcare providers spot conditions like placenta praevia early so precautions can be set up before any bleeding starts. Awesome job completing this session!

question: Which breathing sign is a classic warning of active pulmonary tuberculosis?

options.A: A persistent cough lasting longer than three weeks
options.B: Sudden wheezing and severe shortness of breath
options.C: A sharp, barking cough triggered by cold air
options.D: Copious amounts of clear, watery nasal discharge

explanation: Any cough hanging around for more than three weeks should immediately make you think of TB and prompt a check-up!

question: Why do infectious disease outbreaks often require international teamwork?

options.A: Infectious diseases easily cross national borders and spread globally
options.B: International agencies hold the patent on all known antibiotics
options.C: Local hospitals refuse to treat contagious patients
options.D: National governments lack any interest in stopping local outbreaks

explanation: Viruses and bacteria don't check passports at the border! Because germs spread fast across countries, countries must work together to stop pandemics.

question: Which material is most commonly used to make everyday condoms?

options.A: Cotton
options.B: Silicone
options.C: Leather
options.D: Latex

explanation: You got this! Latex is the go-to material for modern condoms because it is strong, stretchy, and reliable at blocking sperm and infections.

question: A nurse finishes drawing up an emergency medication from a single-dose vial. What should be done with the remaining liquid in the vial?

options.A: Save it in the pocket for the next patient
options.B: Put it back into the main supply drawer
options.C: Discard the leftover portion immediately
options.D: Leave the syringe attached for later use

explanation: Single-dose vials do not contain preservatives, so any leftover medication must be thrown away to prevent microbial growth. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h2)

question: You are getting a stroke survivor ready to go home. What is the best way to involve the family?

options.A: Teach them safe transfer techniques and assess their coping abilities
options.B: Assume they already know how to handle home therapy without guidance
options.C: Tell them to hire paid nurses so they do not have to do any work
options.D: Instruct them to isolate the patient to prevent any accidental injuries

explanation: Giving families practical skills and making sure they feel ready keeps everyone safe and lowers stress at home.

question: What is the main trigger for releasing secretin from the small intestine?

options.A: Unbroken protein chains in the stomach
options.B: Large fat droplets needing emulsification
options.C: Acidic chyme arriving from the stomach
options.D: The sight and smell of favorite foods

explanation: Secretin is released when stomach acid arrives, telling the pancreas to send out bicarbonate to neutralize it.

question: Why are accidental needlestick injuries so scary for healthcare workers?

options.A: They stop the worker from ever touching medical tools again
options.B: They instantly paralyze the hand
options.C: They instantly trigger severe allergies to latex
options.D: They can push infected blood straight into the nurse's bloodstream

explanation: A hollow needle often carries leftover blood from a patient. That's why safe disposal isn't just about the patient—it protects YOU too!

question: Why are financial assistance programs so important for many persons with physical disabilities?

options.A: They prevent extreme poverty caused by limited employment opportunities.
options.B: They replace the need for physical therapy and medical check-ups.
options.C: They cover all luxury expenses and travel costs.
options.D: They guarantee automatic employment in government ministries.

explanation: Financial grants act as a crucial safety net. Because physical disabilities can sometimes make finding stable jobs difficult, this aid helps prevent extreme hardship.

question: How can a fear of side effects lead to drug under-prescription?

options.A: Doctors prescribe double doses to prevent side effects
options.B: Providers choose to omit necessary treatments to avoid potential harm
options.C: Patients stop buying drugs that cause mild stomach upset
options.D: Pharmacists refuse to fill prescriptions for elderly patients

explanation: Exactly! Sometimes being overly scared of side effects stops a practitioner from starting a drug that could actually do the patient a lot of good.

question: You listen to all four areas of a patient's tummy for five full minutes and hear zero sounds. What does this mean?

options.A: Absent bowel sounds indicating decreased motility
options.B: Normal digestion happening very quietly
options.C: Mild gas trapped in the lower colon
options.D: Hyperactive sounds due to recent eating

explanation: Total silence for a full five minutes is a red flag! It usually means the intestines have slowed right down or stopped moving.

question: What is the main advantage of an interprofessional healthcare team for an elderly patient?

options.A: Lower overall healthcare costs for the government
options.B: Comprehensive care that improves overall quality of life
options.C: Faster discharge from acute care hospitals
options.D: Elimination of the need for informal family caregivers

explanation: When different health professionals combine their skills, all aspects of the patient's physical, emotional, and social needs get covered, leading to happier, healthier days.

question: Inside which type of host does a pathogen reach maturity and reproduce sexually?

options.A: Reservoir host
options.B: Accidental host
options.C: Secondary host
options.D: Primary host

explanation: Great job thinking through parasite cycles. The primary (or definitive) host is where the germ finally grows up and completes its sexual reproduction stage.

question: What is the medical term for a lack of oxygen to an unborn baby?

options.A: Placental abruption
options.B: Foetal hyperglycemia
options.C: Intrauterine hypoxia
options.D: Uterine hyperstimulation

explanation: Intrauterine hypoxia refers specifically to the state where a foetus experiences reduced oxygen levels in the womb. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h1)

question: Which condition is a common indication for a musculoskeletal CT scan?

options.A: Acute muscle strains
options.B: Superficial skin lacerations
options.C: Complex bone fractures
options.D: Simple ligament sprains

explanation: CT scans are especially helpful for viewing complicated, multi-part fractures and seeing how bone fragments line up within a joint. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T6#GNS222_U1_T6_h2)

question: A nurse discards an empty glass drug ampoule. Which waste category does this item belong to?

options.A: Food waste
options.B: Sharps
options.C: Paper waste
options.D: General waste

explanation: Even though ampoules are glass rather than needles, their sharp edges can easily cut skin, so they must be treated as sharps waste. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h2)

question: Which of these is a common stereotype that can unfairly hurt female patients?

options.A: Having their physical strength constantly overestimated
options.B: Being labeled as overly emotional or exaggerating pain
options.C: Being discouraged from ever seeking medical help
options.D: Being assumed to always be the primary breadwinner

explanation: Exactly. Dismissing women's physical symptoms as 'just being emotional' is a dangerous trap we must avoid as nurses.

question: What is the main purpose of a clinical guideline in nursing?

options.A: To punish nurses who make minor documentation errors
options.B: To help nurses make evidence-based care decisions
options.C: To increase the cost of hospital equipment purchasing
options.D: To replace doctors completely in the labor room

explanation: Guidelines provide clear, research-backed instructions so nurses know the best steps to take for specific health problems. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h2)

question: Why is assuming a community's health needs based only on past experience a major mistake?

options.A: Every community has unique conditions, and unverified assumptions lead to wasted resources
options.B: Illnesses never repeat themselves in the same geographic location twice
options.C: Community members prefer foreign nurses to local healthcare workers
options.D: Past experience is legally forbidden in public health practice

explanation: Relying on assumptions instead of current local data often results in interventions that do not match real community needs. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h2)

question: Which ethical principle guides a nurse to respect a clear-minded patient who decides to refuse surgery?

options.A: Justice
options.B: Veracity
options.C: Autonomy
options.D: Beneficence

explanation: Autonomy is all about respecting a patient's right to make their own choices about their body and healthcare.

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for the milk ejection or let-down reflex?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Oxytocin makes the tiny muscles around the milk glands contract, squeezing the milk out into the ducts for the baby. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h2)

question: Why do males use the same tube (the urethra) for both urine and semen?

options.A: Both fluids exit the body through the urethra
options.B: The ureters connect directly to the reproductive tract
options.C: The bladder stores semen before ejaculation occurs
options.D: Both fluids are produced together inside the prostate gland

explanation: The male urethra pulls double duty as the final exit path for both urinary and reproductive fluids (though clever internal valves make sure they never mix at the wrong time).

question: Why do we include a reference list at the end of a report?

options.A: To provide extra reading material for hospitalized patients
options.B: To give proper credit to original authors and avoid plagiarism
options.C: To increase the length of the document for academic grading
options.D: To prove that the researcher read every textbook in the library

explanation: Referencing is about honesty—always give credit to the original authors whose work helped you build yours!

question: What is the final step after completing a thorough research critique?

options.A: Firing staff members who do not read journals
options.B: Writing a textbook about research methods
options.C: Throwing away the article because all studies have flaws
options.D: Deciding whether the evidence is strong enough to change clinical practice

explanation: The ultimate purpose of nursing research critique is to determine if and how the findings can safely improve patient care. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h6)

question: How do slow court cases affect the fight against illegal healthcare providers?

options.A: They allow unsafe facilities to continue operating while cases drag on
options.B: They automatically upgrade illegal clinics to accredited status
options.C: They force the government to refund all registration application fees
options.D: They eliminate the need for future facility inspections entirely

explanation: When legal battles take forever in court, these unsafe fake clinics unfortunately get to keep running and endangering people while the case is ongoing.

question: Why do dementia units usually have secure, controlled exits?

options.A: To comply with federal fire safety codes for chemical storage rooms
options.B: To punish residents who refuse to participate in daily group activities
options.C: To restrict family members from visiting outside of strict morning hours
options.D: To prevent wandering and keep residents with memory loss safe

explanation: Correct! Wandering is very common in advanced dementia, so secure doors keep our vulnerable residents safe from getting lost.

question: Which of these is a key thing nurses can do to help with food security?

options.A: Inspecting commercial food processing plants for bacteria
options.B: Operating heavy harvesting machinery on local farms
options.C: Manufacturing nutritional supplements in hospital labs
options.D: Screening patients for hunger and connecting them with resources

explanation: Nurses look out for the whole patient. Asking about food access and linking struggling families to community support programs makes a huge difference.

question: What is the big advantage of a blame-free reporting culture for medication mistakes?

options.A: Encouraging staff to report mistakes so system flaws can be fixed
options.B: Speeding up the time it takes to administer morning medications
options.C: Reducing the hospital budget for pharmaceutical supplies
options.D: Allowing nurses to avoid punishment for deliberate negligence

explanation: When people aren't terrified of punishment, they speak up honestly. That helps the whole team fix broken systems and save lives!

question: What is the primary difference between blunt and penetrating genitourinary trauma?

options.A: Penetrating trauma is caused exclusively by sports-related accidents.
options.B: Blunt trauma always requires immediate emergency surgery.
options.C: Penetrating trauma involves objects breaking through the skin and organ walls.
options.D: Blunt trauma only affects the kidneys and never the external genitalia.

explanation: Penetrating trauma is defined by a foreign object like a knife or bullet entering the body, whereas blunt trauma results from compressive force without an open wound. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h1)

question: What is the first step when a patient's airway is blocked by secretions in a community clinic?

options.A: Applying high-pressure chest compressions
options.B: Starting an immediate intravenous infusion of normal saline
options.C: Clearing the airway using proper positioning and suctioning
options.D: Administering sublingual nitroglycerin tablets

explanation: Airway comes first in every emergency! Positioning the patient and clearing out any blockage gets them breathing easier.

question: Which of the following is NOT a direct consequence of health sector underfunding?

options.A: High rates of nurse migration to foreign countries
options.B: Increased risk of hospital-acquired infections for patients
options.C: Abundant supplies of sterile gloves and modern equipment
options.D: Severe staff shortages and heavy workloads for nurses

explanation: Underfunded facilities always suffer from shortages of basic supplies, not abundance. [learn more](GST322_U4_T2#GST322_U4_T2_h6)

question: A nurse notices dried blood on a clamp coming out of the washer. What should be done?

options.A: The cleaning process was incomplete and the instrument must be re-washed
options.B: The instrument is permanently stained but still safe to use
options.C: The autoclave cycle reached too high a temperature
options.D: The packaging material was sealed incorrectly
